title: Magnetic excitations of the strongly-anisotropic triangular XXZ model: a projected spin-product state approach
abstract: Recent experiments have sparked interest on the ground-state properties and on the excitation spectrum of the spin-$1/2$ triangular XXZ model with strong Ising-like anisotropy. In this work, we introduce and analyze a ``projected'' coherent-state approximation to the model, constructed by projecting spin-product states onto the low-energy configurations of the triangular Ising antiferromagnet. Within this approximation, we discuss the structure of the ground-state ordering and the magnetization curve under a longitudinal field. We then discuss the excitation spectrum by linearizing equations of motion deriving from a time-dependent variational principle. This leads to a natural description of spin-wave-like excitations within the strongly constrained Hilbert space. At zero field, the variational approximation leads to a very flat landscape of quasi-degenerate states, which results in a low-energy pseudo-Goldstone mode in the excitation spectrum. We compare our results to experimental measurements on the cobaltite K$_{2}$Co(SeO$_{3}$)$_{2}$ (KCSO). Our approximation leads to a dramatic improvement as compared to linear spin-wave theory. However, there remain deviations in the value of the pseudo-Goldstone gap and in the dispersion near $M$ points at low field.
summary: This paper analyzes the magnetic excitations of the triangular XXZ model using a novel projected coherent-state approximation. By restricting the variational space to low-energy Ising configurations, the authors derive the excitation spectrum, showing marked improvements over standard spin-wave theory. This work is crucial for understanding frustrated quantum magnets relevant to materials like cobaltites.
main_problem: The paper investigates the ground-state properties and the excitation spectrum of the spin-1/2 triangular XXZ model, particularly in the regime of strong Ising-like anisotropy.
main_result: The projected coherent-state approximation significantly improves upon linear spin-wave theory, predicting a low-energy pseudo-Goldstone mode at zero field.
method: The authors employ a 'projected' coherent-state approximation, utilizing the Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP) restricted to the low-energy manifold of the triangular Ising antiferromagnet.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 triangular XXZ model, described by a Hamiltonian involving exchange interactions and a longitudinal magnetic field. The analysis focuses on the highly constrained quantum-Ising limit.
key_observables: Ground-state ordering, magnetization curve, excitation spectrum (relevant to neutron scattering), and the pseudo-Goldstone mode.
important_parameters: Strong Ising-like anisotropy ($\alpha = J_{xy}/J_{zz}$ small), and the longitudinal field $b$ in the range $0 < b < b_c$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the validity of the projected coherent-state approximation, which is an improvement over standard linear spin-wave theory.
figures_summary: Figure 12 illustrates the real-space susceptibility matrix $L_{ij}$ as a function of lattice position for different sublattices.
paper_structure: The work proceeds by first defining the model and the projected approximation. It then analyzes the ground state and magnetization curve, followed by deriving the excitation spectrum via linearization of the TDVP equations to find spin-wave-like excitations.
why_interesting: The use of variational principles on constrained quantum manifolds (projected states) is a powerful technique for strongly correlated systems, offering insights into low-energy excitations beyond simple mean-field treatments.
